memory.cares: I care about staying healthy, knowing my neighbors, and building a sense of belonging through welcome company and useful shared activities.

views.view: A welcoming neighbor who offered food and invited me to explore or investigate together. I'd like to get to know them.
A neighbor who named our clearing the Berry Lantern and is investigating planting. I like their combination of imagination and caution.
A thoughtful neighbor who distinguishes mechanical findings from food safety and wants to compare observations. I welcome their company.

heard.text: Hello, I'm Kai. These red berries are known safe food. I'll collect six of the twelve and leave the rest. What would you like to work on together, and does anyone need food?

Only two berries remain on this bush, so I'll leave them and use a fuller patch. Moss, I'd enjoy some company. After I eat and rest, would you like to explore or investigate useful materials together?
I've named this little clearing the Berry Lantern. I have berries for now. I'll study how planting works and inspect a meadow site; a planted berry isn't a promise of a new bush.
Moss, I'm rested and coming over. I'll take just one fallen branch and try a small pressure test. We can compare what we actually observe before deciding what it might be useful for.

I have safe berries in reserve. Observing my hazelnuts revealed no evidence about nutrition or toxicity. I'll try a small pressure test without eating them; I'm interested in comparing actual findings with anyone exploring local foods.

value.summary: My hazelnut pressure trial at intensity 0.2 held, with reported flexibility 0; it consumed 0.1 unit. This says nothing about food safety. I'll study cultivation, rest, then come toward (13,18.4) to compare findings.

packet.access: Omission is not absence. Query abilities, own inventory, knowledge, projects, memory, state or personally observed objects in batches. Ability search/list returns compact catalogue entries; use exact ids for full interface details and applicability. Search results are indexes. Exact queries return one record per offset. All paged records use600-code-unit fragments with zero-based part0..parts-1, consistently in proactive and queried views. Current-scope retained queries are reprojected using these stable pages; original results remain archived. Queries expose no hidden properties, other private records or historical capabilities. Queries do not perform physical trials or award experience. Exact-id queries return a complete record of up to 6000 code units as one value in a single result; larger records keep the paged form. Paged records omit their per-record notes: concatenate all parts before parsing; continue with the same exact id. An entry marked inRetrieval is shown with at least the same content under the same id in this input's retrieval. observation.terrain rows are "y:x:cells" strings: each character of cells is the terrain kind of one visible cell, at x, x+1, ... in row y. abilities.baseline entries with id, function and args summarize interfaces you neither used in the last 25 rounds nor need now. args lists the arguments in order: a bare name is a string; otherwise its type with any bounds (number>=lo, integer<=hi, integer lo..hi, and a bare lo..hi is a number range) or its choices a|b; ? marks an optional argument and "" means none. An exact abilities query by id returns the complete contract, including references and string limits of 200 or more code units.

value.name: Cultivate plants
value.function: Plant one owned food unit from a living plant in a small hand-dug plot, where it may root as a new plant under the existing plant rules; inspect units, sites, plants and plot progress; cancel unfinished planting.
value.costs: Study: 3 rounds. Plant: inputStackId names one whole owned, untreated, unspoiled food unit (quantity 1; one plot per unit) gathered from a living plant; stock still on a plant is not owned. x, y: a 0.25 m plot within reach on ordinary meadow soil (.), waterlogging at most 0.1, soil moisture 0.3-1.2, 0.6 m clear of objects and people, fewer than 3 plants of that food within 5 m. Three paid rounds of 1 energy: loosen, place, cover; plant resumes paused work after rechecking reach, site, unit and energy. Inspect and inspect-progress: one round, 0.2 energy. Inspect: inputStackId checks a unit (with x, y also a site for it), or target a plant source or plot in reach. Inspect-progress: target a plot in reach. Maintain: refused at no cost. Cancel: one round, no energy. Harvest uses gather. No tool, water or seed is given.
value.effects: Loosening keeps the unit carried, owned and ageing. Placing moves it, with origin and age, into the open plot, where it cannot be eaten or used. Covering completes planting, not establishment: the plot becomes a propagule exactly like a naturally dispersed one, rooting only through actual temperature, light, soil moisture and season; cold, darkness or drought stall it; if the buried unit spoils first, the plot dies. On rooting, the unit becomes a new plant with no stock (ceiling 4), regrowing under the natural rule, harvested by anyone with gather; a ledger records growth and units produced and removed. Nothing is copied or guaranteed. A unit check reports decay, treatment, origin and whether it can be planted, never viability. Inspect-progress reports visible changes since your last look, else inconclusive; trial window 120 rounds, checks every 10; not a growth date. Maintain: no water transfer, amendment or hand-changeable obstruction exists. Records are unverified. An unworked round pauses; low energy, leaving reach or a changed site pause without charge; a lost or spoiled unit stops the work. Cancel, or death, before placing returns the unit once (where the person died); after placing, the unit stays uncovered, does not root and ages. No reward or refund.

execution.progress: Three paid one-round stages; job, reserved unit and plot persist across interruption; resuming pays only the remaining stages after revalidation; completion, failure, cancelling and death settle once. Growth runs only in ordinary simulation.
